title: Output-tape return step at a symbol
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Boolean Turing machine, let $x,y$ be Boolean words, and fix an encoded selector, a simulated configuration $c$ on input $x$, auxiliary tape contents and head positions, a position $P$ on input $y$, an output register $r$, and a Boolean tag $b$. If the output tape contains the bit $v$ at its current head position $z_O$, then one step of the tabulating machine from the lifted state with control state $\mathrm{wret}$ leaves the other data and output tape unchanged, keeps the control state at $\mathrm{wret}$, and moves the output-tape head from $z_O$ to $z_O-1$.
hypotheses_covered: auxiliary tape contents $\tau_C,\tau_O$ and head positions $z_C,z_O$
